sections.title: Around Town
sections.content: A city is mostly nouns, and you already know how to put an article in front of them. The one new word here is 'hay' — it means both 'there is' and 'there are', it is a single fixed word, and it is how you say what a place has in it. It is followed by 'un', 'una', a number, or nothing at all.

items.spanish: Hay un mercado en el centro.
items.english: There's a market in the centre.
Are there always this many people?

items.spanish: Los sábados hay mucha gente en el barrio antiguo.
items.english: On Saturdays there are lots of people in the old quarter.

sections.content: 'Hay' never changes. One lake or twenty, it stays the same word: 'hay un lago', 'hay muchos lagos'. There is no 'hays' and no 'hayn'.
